status: architecture audit; proposed release contract, not a deployed schema migration
question: Which published representations and implementations can support independent, evidence-grounded extraction of genomics assay workflows that later support comparison, atlas construction and search?
ambiguity_class: representation semantics: changing node identity, state boundaries or flow meaning changes the scientific assertions and comparisons
input: A declared method implementation/variant, its registered primary methods, supplements and applicable dependencies, including original-to-rendition provenance and source availability limits.
output: The existing source-scoped Workflow plus its bound evidence, source review, coverage and restrictions, independently usable without a concept registry or atlas.
not_identified_by_input: An actual historical execution trace or successful laboratory replication
Undocumented reaction chemistry, intermediate composition, material fate or numerical defaults
Cross-method equivalence, compatibility or ancestry merely from a shared name, reagent, embedding score or topology
The globally optimal operation granularity or a universal assay stage taxonomy
required_invariants: Source and variant identity survive extraction, admission and query.
An operation occurrence and its material/data state are distinct from reusable operation concepts and actual execution events.
Material flow, data flow, precedence and conditional control retain different meanings; source array order alone supplies none of them.
Individual claim/connection support and restrictions remain addressable; a positive comparison cannot upgrade the underlying Workflow.
Different legitimate local decompositions may retain the same consequential facts, interfaces and branch semantics.
Graph construction and indexing may add reviewed annotations but may not silently alter published extraction artifacts.
A source-access gap, an omitted available fact, a source-silent fact and a contradicted assertion remain distinguishable.
A search miss is not a scientific negative; an unmatched local operation is retained.
alternatives: Adopt a universal executable laboratory-action language as the extraction ontology.
Extract unconstrained triples and canonicalize labels into one shared graph.
Retain a small fixed workflow grammar with source-specific descriptions; compare explicit regions and add reviewed shared definitions afterward.
selected_direction: The third alternative. Adapt LabOP flow/plan semantics and protocol-NLP annotation principles; use EDC-style retrieval and contextual mapping downstream. Keep the existing Workflow contract and harden its release boundary before broad refactoring.
verification_plan: Evaluate source-to-record omission coverage separately from record-to-source claim support.
Probe material-versus-data handoffs, same-label different-state identity, parallel versus alternative branches, negation, variant mixing, kit delegation and readout/decoding dependencies.
Require unsupported injected clauses to remain rejected in extraction, atlas admission and query, even if another property of their operation supports a mapping.
Compare required facts and answers to source-grounded queries under paraphrase and reasonable grouping changes; do not require identical node counts.
Measure coverage and false-match rates separately for downstream candidate retrieval and scientific membership review.
Report elapsed time, source reads, repair count and provider token counts per phase alongside scientific errors.
implementation_status: Read-only code/paper audit and documentation. No new model run, production dependency, schema version or acceptance rule is installed by this record.
